scope: Optimized WAT for all passing modules; default-tier V8 disassembly diagnostic runs for sum and diviter only. Static instruction sites are not dynamic allocation counts.

findings.repetition: Outer repeat workers retain dynamic I64 count comparison, kernel work and an incremented tail call. Kernels retain their recurrence, arithmetic, pointer traversal or allocation. Numeric imports provide runtime values. List barrier does not obscure a known value; prepared list globals come from native runtime input.
findings.sum: function1 retains I64 decrement/add, environment cast, readiness and closure loads, then return_call. TurboFan function1 retains these checks and tail jump; function3 retains outer count branch, scalar identity import, closure allocation, sum work and incremented tail jump.
findings.diviter: function3 retains repeated division/list construction and incremented outer tail call. function5 retains two cdr loads and struct.new before recursive tail transfer. TurboFan confirms bump allocation and tail jump, not a reused final answer.
findings.takl_ntakl: Binaryen removes unused element fields; the recursive list type contains only its next reference. This is valid dead-field optimization, not equal physical allocation layout to Chez.
findings.cpstak: Native scalar values remain unboxed, but generated continuations contain separate closure/environment objects and captured recursive-binding readiness cells.
findings.fib: Binaryen inlines recursive branches extensively; the optimized I64 module is 50,344 bytes, F64 module70,336 bytes. Timing alone does not isolate the impact of inlining.
